newsitem.title: USA: TIAA-CREF assets rise $25 bln to $185.3 bln in '96.
newsitem.headline: TIAA-CREF assets rise $25 bln to $185.3 bln in '96.

text.p: Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association-College Retirement Equities Fund (TIAA CREF) said Tuesday assets it manages rose 16 percent or by almost $25 billion to $185.3 billion at yearend 1996 from about $160.6 billion a year ago.
TIAA-CREF, the nationwide retirement system for educators, said $86.4 billion of the assets were invested in private placements, publicly-traded bonds, commercial mortgages and real estate.

The remaining $98.9 billion were in seven CREF variable annuity investment accounts, including CREF Stock, Global Equities, Growth, Money Market, Bond Market, Social Choice, and Equity Index Accounts, it said.

The system's combined 1996 total revenue, derived from premiums received, investment income, and realized capital gains, was $24.3 billion, up 34 percent or $6.2 billion from $18.1 billion in 1995, said John Biggs, chairman and chief executive.

In 1996, 100,000 new members joined TIAA-CREF, raising membership to 1.85 million people at 6,100 colleges, universities, teaching hospitals, independent schools, and related nonprofit education and research groups in the United States, it said.
It said the statutory capital of TIAA, a legal reserve life insurance and annuity company, increased to $6.9 billion, giving it a total statutory capital ratio of 8.7 percent.
TIAA's individual life insurance in force at yearend 1996 was $34.7 billion, up from $32.7 billion the year before.
For 1996, TIAA issued $3.3 billion in new individual life insurance and another $3.3 billion to existing policyholders under its renewable cost-of-living insurance provision.
CREF, registered as an open-end diversified management investment company, is invested in stocks of over 4,000 companies in the U.S. and in 35 foreign countries.

During 1996, Biggs said, TIAA-CREF members allocated 58 percent of total pension premiums among the five equity-based CREF variable accounts. About 42 percent were placed among the TIAA traditional annuity, the TIAA Real Estate Account, and the CREF variable bond and money market accounts, it said.
"This marked a further shift in premium dollars toward equities during a period of excellent stock market performance," he said.

"We would expect to see some shift back to TIAA in a rising interest rate environment, or in a declining stock market. But we also expect participants to continue making allocation choices that look beyond short-term trends in the financial markets."
By charter, TIAA-CREF operates on a nonprofit basis, with all contingency reserves held for the benefit of participants.
